newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CAM overstated profits for 4 yrs - auditors.
newsitem.headline: CAM overstated profits for 4 yrs - auditors.

text.p: Accountants Price Waterhouse said on Friday precision engineering company CAM International Holdings Ltd had entered into a series of "questionable" deals with non-group entities over a four-year period from 1993.

The accountants, appointed after Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) white-collar crime bureau began a fraud probe into CAM's affairs, said these deals appeared designed to conceal the company's true financial performance.

"The effect of these transactions was to overstate the operating profits of the group by Singapore $13.2 million in financial year 1993, S$9.1 million in 1994, S$20.6 million in 1995 and S$14.1 million in 1996," Price Waterhouse said in a report commissioned by CAM's directors.

The CAD has charged CAM's ex-managing director and chief executive Raymond Chew with criminal breach of trust for misappropriating Singapore $1.45 million of company funds and on 12 counts of falsifying accounts and of abetment of forgery.
An ex-auditor of the company, Cheong Khee San, has also been charged on three counts of forgery.

Price Waterhouse said the company made payments between the group and various non-group entities to make the questionable transactions appear genuine. Fictitious documents were created to support such payments in some cases.
Price Waterhouse said CAM was now experiencing a cash flow problem, which it said would get worse if additional funding from outside the company did not materialise.
It said a proposed investment in CAM by Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd would alleviate, but not remedy, the cash flow problem.

"It is therefore imperative for the group to immediately explore all alternative options to raise funds. In the meantime, the group's management should waste no time to secure the support of its bankers, creditors, suppliers, customers and partners," the report said.
In a separate statement, CAM's board of directors said it had just received a copy of the Price Waterhouse report and was reviewing its contents.
